topics.title: Artwork across borrower and companion apps
topics.body: The active saved theme’s sidebar PNG also decorates borrower catalog/account/reading headers, the librarian PWA and Android library banner. It is cropped to fit each banner with a readability tint; book cards stay clear. Artwork is public branding, so never upload private information. Selecting a plain theme removes the previous image; selecting a saved theme restores that theme’s artwork. Existing portrait uploads work without re-uploading. Refresh browser pages or refresh Android to receive a changed appearance. The public root welcome page retains its original artwork/layout but has no Install / add browser app button. Borrower installation remains under Account → This device and on the shared catalog. Librarian PWA installation and native Android installation/pairing options are unchanged.

topics.title: Suggest books and series for the library to buy
topics.body: Anyone with the enabled shared library link can select Suggest a book or series to buy without signing in. Choose Book or Series, enter the title and optionally author, ISBN and a short reason (up to 1500 characters). A series does not need an ISBN; any supplied ISBN must be valid. Suggestions are private to librarians, not publicly listed and not associated with your account, contact details or encrypted reading list. Do not include contact information or private reading notes. Approved accounts also have the button next to Catalog filters; their encrypted list may remain locked. Pending accounts can return to their shared link. Sending a suggestion does not reserve a copy, start a loan, create a catalog entry or guarantee a purchase. Admins on the server/iPhone PWA open Books to buy from Quick Actions or Settings & Tools → Books & Organization; Reader purchase suggestions is inside that tool. Android has the same section in Books to buy. Pending suggestions appear in the admin bell and optional admin request alerts. Keep for consideration or Decline changes review status and clears its pending alert. Delete suggestion requires confirmation and permanently removes it from the current server. Older complete backups may retain it; ask the librarian to remove a suggestion if needed because it is not tied to your account. The inbox is limited to 500 retained suggestions; librarians can delete reviewed items to free space. Submission attempts are rate limited and retries with the same request ID avoid duplicates. Complete server backups include suggestions; library-only JSON exports do not. The existing private Books to buy wishlist stays separate and requires a valid book ISBN before adding an owned copy.

topics.title: Why create a borrower account? It is optional
topics.body: The first shared catalog page explains that you can browse, request a book and suggest an acquisition without an account. Create account / Sign in is optional and free. A personal account adds your own To Be Read (TBR) list, reading tracker, reading history, loan/request management and available renewal controls. Personal reading lists and notes use the existing encrypted private-list system with a separate private passphrase and recovery code; they are not librarian acquisition suggestions. Librarian approval is required before account features are available. Sign-in and registration screens repeat the explanation and offer Continue without an account when opened with a shared library link. Borrowing and reading status stay separate. A TBR entry is not a hold or loan.

topics.title: Admin notification bell — all attention items
topics.body: On the server dashboard, paired iPhone/browser companion and Android companion, the bell opens Admin notifications. Its badge totals pending account approvals, pending book requests, pending renewal requests, pending purchase suggestions, approved/ready holds awaiting handover, overdue active loans, restored-access review, portable-backup errors, unconfirmed enabled email-reminder deliveries and push-delivery warnings. Review opens the existing relevant tool with its safeguards. Opening the bell does not dismiss tasks: resolving their cause removes them after refresh. Returned loans and blocked/approved accounts are excluded. Server/PWA refresh about every 15 seconds when no form is open and on focus; Android checks about every 30 seconds while foregrounded, after changes and on Refresh notifications. Failed refresh keeps the last list with an unavailable warning; it is not proof there are no alerts. No borrower private reading/vault data or contact details are read into the notification summaries. Optional admin PWA push additionally covers new account, book, renewal and purchase requests, checked each minute; native Android background admin alerts use periodic checks around every 15 minutes and may be delayed by Android. Neither replaces the full bell inbox. Android needs the updated companion APK; server/PWA updates do not replace native Android code.

topics.title: Install the borrower or librarian web app
topics.body: Use the public HTTPS library hostname with a browser-trusted certificate in regular Chrome, or Safari on iPhone. The plain public welcome page has no install button. Borrowers can install from the shared catalog or Account → This device; these installation controls remain available. The librarian /companion/ pairing page offers Install / add librarian app; after pairing the control is under Settings & Tools → People & Access in This companion. Chrome uses its native install prompt when available. Otherwise use Chrome menu → Add to Home screen → Install; desktop Chrome may place Install page as app under Cast, save and share. Create shortcut alone is not an app installation. A private-IP http:// address, certificate warning, Incognito/in-app browser, existing installation or Chrome installation service policy can prevent an install prompt. Close old tabs, reopen the HTTPS address and refresh after an update; no data clearing or unpairing is required. If only a shortcut remains, report the exact address and browser version. On iPhone: Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → Open as Web App if shown → Add. Install the librarian companion before pairing where possible. Addresses without a trailing slash redirect safely. The welcome page never reveals a private catalog token. Borrower and librarian apps keep distinct stable identities. Installation grants no new access; private account and pairing authorization remain required. Offline pages explain reconnection; private records/API responses are not cached by service workers.

topics.title: Library analytics & insights — optional and private by design
topics.body: Open Settings & Tools → Data & History → Analytics & insights on the server, paired iPhone PWA or Android companion. It has its own settings page; the dashboard/Home no longer contains an analytics panel. Analytics is off until an administrator enables it. Choose 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or All time; the metric selector charts website page loads, catalog views, book-detail opens, catalog searches, zero-result searches, requests, checkouts, returns and copies added. These are aggregate activity counts, not unique people. Popular books are ranked by public catalog detail opens. No visitor identifier, IP address, search term, account name/contact, URL token or encrypted reading information is stored. Browser Do Not Track / Global Privacy Control preferences suppress public telemetry. Analytics stays on this server, protected at rest and included in complete backups; it is not sent to Carribrary developers. Collection starts when enabled, not retroactively. Daily charts keep 730 buckets; all-time totals continue. Popularity has a bounded distinct-book budget (1000 books per day and 10000 all time), so counts for additional distinct titles may be omitted. Pausing stops new collection and retains existing aggregates; clearing requires CLEAR ANALYTICS and never deletes library or reading records. Deleting circulation history does not automatically change anonymous past activity counts. On recovery rehearsal/local review analytics is not collected. Website page loads counts successful welcome, shared-catalog and borrower account entry pages; it does not track private reading tab activity.

topics.title: Page progress and rereading history
topics.body: Reading Tracker / My reading → Edit reading: enter current page and total pages, with 0 for an unknown total. Whole pages from 0 to 100000 are accepted; current cannot exceed a known total. A known total shows an automatic percentage/progress bar; finishing sets current to total. Under Sessions, quotes & notes choose Start a reread after finishing. This preserves the earlier session start/finish dates, page progress, rating and notes, then opens a fresh current read. Earlier sessions are read-only history. The current read remains editable; use Start a reread rather than replacing the dates of a finished record when beginning again. Up to 1000 earlier sessions are supported per reading entry. Removing a reading entry removes its earlier sessions and book annotations after confirmation. Clearing finished history also removes earlier completed sessions from an active reread while preserving the active read and its book-level annotations. Reading and borrowing are separate; finishing a book does not return a loan. Server and paired iPhone PWA share these controls; native Android has the same page fields, session view and reread confirmation.

topics.title: Reading goals, statistics and optional completion streak
topics.body: Inside Reading Tracker / My reading, choose a summary year and Reading goal. Set 0 to remove the selected year goal, or 1–10000 books (years 1900–2200). Each dated finished session, including rereads, counts toward that year. Monthly summaries show completed reads and pages; yearly summaries preserve multiple years. Page counts use the total length of finished reads, or recorded current pages where total is unknown. Unknown page lengths are not guessed; these summaries do not infer daily pages from a last-known position. Undated finishes remain in history but are excluded from date-based totals. Genres are counted where catalog metadata supplies one; missing genres are marked Not recorded. Administrators can optionally enter genre in book details. The optional completion-streak detail counts consecutive dates with a completed book, not inferred daily reading. Household profiles are visible to household administrators. Borrower account goals/statistics are calculated in the unlocked client from the encrypted vault, never in librarian analytics.

topics.title: Favorite quotes and page-linked private notes
topics.body: Add a book to the reading list, then open Sessions, quotes & notes. Choose Favorite quote or Personal note, enter up to 4000 characters and optionally a whole page number from 1 to 100000. Saved passages remain associated with the book across rereads, while each read preserves its own overall notes/rating. Individual annotations can be deleted with confirmation. Quote and page-note limits are 1000 annotations per book. Borrower account passages, notes, page progress, reread sessions and annual goals stay inside the existing encrypted personal vault; librarians cannot view them through admin pages, APIs or exports. Unlock with the private passphrase, not the sign-in password. Encrypted personal backup/restore includes these fields. Remember the separate recovery code: the librarian cannot recover it. The existing limitation remains: the server delivers the browser code, so this protects stored data rather than a malicious server owner modifying that code.

topics.title: 2.0.47 data migration and recovery boundary
topics.body: This release upgrades library format 5 to format 6 to preserve reading progress, reread sessions, goals and annotations. Existing reading and circulation records stay in place; a private pre-upgrade snapshot is retained. Credentials remain format 2. Older server executables cannot open format 6 and must not be used to write it. Program-only rollback is restricted to compatible 2.0.47–2.0.50 programs; use guided complete restoration for earlier supported data. Guided complete recovery accepts supported 2.0.43/44 format-4, 2.0.45/46 format-5 and 2.0.47 format-6 sources, subject to portable/machine-bound protections. Keep a complete backup before upgrading. Android JSON restore accepts format 6 as well as older supported formats.

topics.title: Portable backup — recover onto a replacement computer
topics.body: All newly created complete server backups are portable format 2. Carribrary copies its server encryption keys into the password-encrypted archive while leaving the live keyring unchanged. Windows recovered keys are protected for the destination machine. Keep the archive password separately; it cannot be reset. Borrower private-list passphrases/recovery codes are still required and are not replaced by the archive password. This includes account databases and server pairing identities, library records and saved settings; existing deletion/revocation history rewinds to the snapshot. Source library/credential formats are 6/2 in 2.0.47. New portable archives need Carribrary 2.0.47 or later to read them; 2.0.45/46 cannot unpack format-2 archives or open format-6 library data. Older format-1 Windows archives remain machine-bound; they cannot be converted after the original computer is lost. Create a new portable archive while the old computer works. Custom nonstandard encryption providers can require supervised recovery and are rejected rather than silently called portable. No archive/password is sent to the developer. The password-encrypted archive contains sensitive identity/key material: anyone with both the file and password can recover its server data.

topics.title: Weekly portable backups — keep four
topics.body: Server/iPhone PWA: Settings & Tools → Data & History → Portable replacement backup, also linked in Backups and Setup & updates. Android: Settings & Tools → Data & History → Weekly portable backups. Turn on the seven-day schedule, choose/confirm a 12–128 character archive password, and accept retention of four completed automatic archives. The schedule password is protected on the server so unattended backups can run; status never reveals it. Blank password fields preserve the saved password. Changing the password affects future archives only: keep old passwords for old files. The server checks every 15 minutes and on startup; it must be running. First backup is due after enabling; Create scheduled backup now runs it immediately. Before publishing each new file and removing any old file, Carribrary checks the new archive. It keeps four managed automatic archives and deletes the oldest after successful creation; failure retains the completed copies. Only fixed-name Carribrary-managed files in its portable-backups directory are rotated. Downloaded/manual copies are never removed. Download latest portable backup to another computer, an external drive or your own cloud storage. Copies on the same server drive alone do not protect against drive/computer loss. Managed location is the private server data folder / portable-backups. No arbitrary external folder or cloud upload is configured by this feature. Backups have the existing 2 GB / 10,000-file limit and exclude prior archives, program binaries and external proxy/OS configuration. After historical restoration the old automatic schedule is paused and must be deliberately configured again. Ordinary automatic library snapshots are also bounded: at most 16 recent scheduled catalog snapshots and seven daily snapshots. These smaller snapshots exclude account credentials and borrower vaults and do not replace complete portable backups. User-named/manual and migration safety snapshots are not automatically rotated; installation-managed Windows recovery points retain their separate explicit cleanup tool.

topics.title: Restore onto a new computer — guided steps
topics.body: Before replacement, create/download a current portable complete archive, verify it and keep its password separately off the old computer. On the replacement computer install Carribrary 2.0.47 or later. Open Complete Backup Recovery from the server computer application menu/Windows Start menu, choose the archive and enter its password. Verification reports portable or legacy machine-bound protection. Run the isolated recovery test, sign in with credentials in the archive and inspect books, borrowers and loans. Then use the existing checked warnings and exact RESTORE LIBRARY confirmation. Retain the new installation data until recovery succeeds. The wizard protects keys for the new host, prepares the Windows service HTTPS identity when needed, and retains the target data folder. Remote access, discovery and historical notifications/schedules stay paused for local administrator review. Review accounts and paired devices, record the review and resume using the wizard. Configure the new computer LAN address/router forwarding, DuckDNS updater and HTTPS/Caddy separately. Existing paired identities can be retained if the address/hostname is reachable; changed addresses can require a connection update or re-pairing. Do not run two live servers with the same restored identity. Stop or retire the old server when switching over. External certificates/services/tasks and environment-only secrets are not a full computer image and are not recreated by a data backup. Physical Windows/Linux/Pi migration still needs target-system checks; integrity verification alone does not certify a machine move.

topics.title: Library & Appearance — identity and theme together
topics.body: Library & Appearance now has two cards. Library identity saves the library name, icon, banner subtitle and encouraging saying together. Blank sayings are hidden; transparent icons are preserved. Theme & artwork combines builtin color presets, saved custom themes, color pickers/hex fields and sidebar PNG upload/preview/removal. Changes are drafts until Apply preset or Save & use theme. Builtin presets apply their colors and clear artwork. Saved custom themes restore their own colors and saved PNG, or clear the overlay if they have no image. New theme clears the draft name and image; current colors can be the starting point. Use current library artwork deliberately copies the active overlay. PNG uploads affect only the draft until saved. Old name/icon/sayings/colors/overlay bookmarks route to these consolidated pages. Existing saved themes and images are preserved. Google Books integration is under Books & Organization; notification status stays under Borrowing & Reminders. Unrelated buttons under the old sayings form are removed. Artwork and identity are public library branding; do not include private data.

topics.title: Quick Actions and lending limits
topics.body: Dashboard Quick Actions includes Share Library and Books to Buy, alongside Add Book, Create Hold, Batch Checkout and Backup Now. Both tools keep their settings cards under Books & Organization. Android Home has Share library and Books to buy quick actions too. The library share QR is for borrowers; private administrator pairing is a different tool. Lending limits no longer has a separate settings card: open Lending & Holds → Lending limits. Batch and per-borrower limits, return behavior and existing safety confirmations are unchanged.

topics.title: New theme clears the artwork draft
topics.body: Custom themes save their own colors and sidebar artwork together. In Library & Appearance → Theme & artwork, selecting a saved theme loads its colors, name and saved PNG (or its saved no-artwork choice). New theme clears the name and artwork preview, keeping the displayed colors as a starting point; it does not inherit the previous theme's PNG. The live library and saved themes change only when you save. Use current library artwork deliberately copies the active overlay into this draft. Save & use theme stores that choice with the new colors. Returning to an existing saved theme loads its own artwork again. Closing without saving leaves the library unchanged. Android Colors & custom themes has the same New theme reset; selecting a named theme also loads its draft, while phone color selection stays local until published. Library/credential formats are 6/2 in this release; a pre-upgrade snapshot protects existing data. Compatible program-only recovery supports 2.0.47.

topics.title: Saved custom themes include sidebar artwork — format 5
topics.body: A named custom theme now saves its colors together with a sidebar PNG or an explicit no-artwork choice. Server/iPhone PWA: Settings & Tools → Library & Appearance → Theme & artwork. The editor previews the saved image. Use current library artwork captures the current overlay; No artwork for this theme saves an empty choice. Save & use applies both colors and artwork. Selecting a different saved custom theme restores its own image; a saved empty choice clears the previous overlay. Saving or removing a PNG in Theme & artwork while a custom theme is active also updates that theme. Built-in color presets clear the sidebar overlay when applied. Android Colors & custom themes provides current-artwork/no-artwork choices when saving/editing. Native phone preset selection remains local; Apply selected theme to shared library applies the saved theme and artwork to the shared server. Sidebar images appear where the layout has a sidebar; narrow phone layouts remain responsive. Older themes had no stored artwork choice: selecting one without a saved artwork choice now clears the overlay; explicitly choose and save its artwork to associate it. There is no guess about which image historically belonged to an old theme. On first startup, Carribrary keeps a private pre-theme-art-v5 library backup and upgrades to library format 5; copies, loans, accounts, pairing and vaults are preserved. Older format-4 programs would discard per-theme artwork, so compatible program-only recovery is restricted to 2.0.47. Do not downgrade live format-5 data with an earlier installer. The Complete Backup Recovery wizard accepts supported 2.0.43/2.0.44 format-4 archives as well as 2.0.45/2.0.46 format-5 archives and tests their upgrade in the separate rehearsal. Credential format remains 2. Each stored PNG keeps the existing 512 × 1536 / 2 MB limit (legacy 512 × 256 is accepted); multiple themed images increase export/cache size. Use a complete backup when a library JSON export exceeds the existing 10 MB JSON restore limit. Artwork is public branding: do not put private information in it.

topics.title: Complete Backup Recovery — Windows, Linux/Flatpak and Raspberry Pi
topics.body: Create and keep a complete .carribrary-backup archive and its password before an update. To open the independent recovery wizard on Windows use Start → Carribrary → Complete Backup Recovery or the tray entry; approve administrator access. On Linux/Flatpak use Carribrary Complete Backup Recovery in the application menu or the Recovery action on the Carribrary launcher. Pi desktop has the same named application entry and requests administrator authorization. Backups and Data & History → Complete Backup Recovery explain the launchers; Open installed recovery wizard uses the installed carribrary-recovery: handler on the server computer. If a browser cannot open it, use the application menu. Phone companions cannot run an operating-system recovery launcher. The local browser wizard works without starting the working dashboard, provided the installed executable and operating-system permissions still work. A damaged executable may first require installer repair. Choose your complete archive, enter its password and Verify backup. The file is uploaded only to the local loopback helper, checked and privately unpacked. The helper uses a one-time launch capability and short-lived private session, not a public recovery URL or a first-visitor administrator signup. Refreshing its browser page keeps the existing session. It never requires your archive password in a command or sends your archive to the developer. Wrong-password, damaged and incompatible backups are rejected. Guided testing/restoration supports same-platform 2.0.43/2.0.44 format-4 archives or 2.0.45/2.0.46 format-5 archives; Legacy Windows archives need the original computer. New format-2 portable archives support a replacement host. Earlier-format archives can be integrity-verified but require supervised compatible recovery. Next choose Start recovery test. Open the separate test address in InPrivate/Incognito, sign in with the administrator credentials in the backup and check books, borrowers and loans. The test has a RECOVERY TEST banner, separate login cookies, local-only listeners and disabled automatic email/push/discovery. Borrower vaults still need their own private-list passphrase/recovery code. Stop test ends only that disposable copy. For live restoration, check the rehearsal/warning boxes and type RESTORE LIBRARY exactly. Windows/Pi stop their matching managed service. Flatpak users must first use the normal authenticated Stop confirmation on the working dashboard; restoration refuses a still-open data folder. Current data is retained as a complete private before-restore folder before replacement. Current program, connection configuration and external HTTPS/Caddy certificates/service definitions stay separate; supplied archive configuration is available in the original archive and temporary private staging until Finish. A failed startup attempts to put the retained current folder back, preserving failed data too. If a restore or undo is interrupted, reopen the wizard and use Undo interrupted restore, typing UNDO RESTORE. Keep all retained folders/journal if it cannot finish; never merge individual databases or delete them to force startup. Restoration rewinds old accounts, deleted data, passwords, device revocations and loans. Remote access and automatic notifications are therefore held locally after successful restore; follow Review restored access before going online. Finish / close recovery tool stops its rehearsal and removes normal temporary upload/test files; closing only the tab does not stop the helper. Retained old/failed folders remain private. A crash can leave protected temporary sessions for support to clean up. Allow space for the archive, verified copy, test copy, new restored copy and retained entire current data. Current archive limits remain 2 GB / 10,000 files. This is not an operating-system image, cross-machine DPAPI migration or automatic older-program rollback.

topics.title: Review restored access before resuming remote connections
topics.body: After Complete Backup Recovery restores historical data, the server starts local-only. Phone/public access, discovery and background notification workers remain paused even across restarts until a local administrator records a review. Open the restored local dashboard from the wizard, sign in using credentials in the restored backup, and review Borrower accounts, Dashboard administrators, Android phone pairing and iPhone/browser pairing. Older snapshots may bring back access that you previously blocked or revoked: revoke/block/remove it again where needed. Select Record local review in the restored-library banner, confirm that you checked accounts/devices and type RESUME REMOTE ACCESS exactly. Only a password-authenticated local administrator session may record this; paired tokens cannot bypass it. Return to the wizard, choose Check local review status if needed, then Restart after local review. Flatpak users must again confirm Stop on the working local dashboard before that restart. Normal remote access resumes using current connection settings. Email and push configuration from the backup was retained under paused filenames; deliberately configure email and request notification permissions again after reviewing borrowers/devices. No automatic messages are sent simply because an older archive was restored. Do not blindly retry cached pending companion changes after a historical restore; refresh and review them first. Program-only recovery is blocked while the local review marker remains. If you finish the wizard early, reopen it after completing the local review to restart. Keep retained folders private: they can contain historical credentials and deleted records.

topics.title: Headless Raspberry Pi recovery and custom service layouts
topics.body: Pi desktop users open Carribrary Complete Backup Recovery from the application menu; no recovery commands are needed there. A headless Pi needs an SSH terminal because it has no local screen/browser. Run sudo home-library-recovery over SSH. It opens a loopback-only helper and prints a private RECOVERY-OPEN URL with a temporary token; do not share it. From your desktop computer create an SSH local port tunnel using the printed port: ssh -L PORT:127.0.0.1:PORT YOUR_USER@YOUR_PI. Replace PORT twice with the helper port and YOUR_USER/YOUR_PI with the normal SSH login/address. Keep both SSH sessions open, then open the printed localhost URL in the desktop browser. Select the backup using that browser file picker and follow the same wizard. Do not forward the recovery port on the router or bind it publicly. Administrator authorization is required to stop/start the home-library service and restore correct home-library ownership. The guided Pi flow supports the packaged /var/lib/home-library service data layout; customized data paths/unit overrides need supervised recovery rather than guessed file replacement. Flatpak uses its own sandbox data location and host-browser file selection through local upload, without permanent broad filesystem grants. A Linux archive can be considered across Linux architectures when its source version/format are supported, but operating-system/service/external configuration is not automatically migrated.

topics.title: Verify complete backup — check before you need it
topics.body: Server and iPhone companion: Settings & Tools → Data & History → Verify complete backup (also linked from Backups). Android: Settings → Data & History → Verify complete backup. Choose your saved .carribrary-backup file, enter its 12–128 character backup password and select Verify saved backup. The file uploads privately to your own server. Carribrary checks authenticated encryption, every manifest file/hash and SQLite integrity in protected temporary storage, then removes the temporary upload and recovered copy. It never restores, merges or edits live records. The report gives archive date, original server version/platform, library format and checked file count/size; it does not show keys, filenames, contacts or borrower private content. Password and file selection are not stored in app preferences. Choose the file again to verify another backup; keep the original file and password safely on a separate drive. Wrong-password, damaged, truncated, busy or timed-out checks do not prove a backup is valid; read the error, check server free space and retry. Only one verification runs at a time. Up to 2 GB of original data / 10,000 files; encrypted uploads have a bounded overhead allowance. Allow space for the encrypted upload, decrypted ZIP and recovered files together. Keep the page/app open; verification has an eight-minute server budget and some proxies impose shorter upload limits. Closing/disconnecting can interrupt verification. Cleanup runs on normal completion/failure/cancellation; a server crash can leave an administrator-protected temporary folder, excluded from future backups, for support to remove. For a large file or a server that will not open, use the included executable with --verify-complete-backup ARCHIVE; it prompts privately for the password and does not start the server or restore data. Verification is an integrity check, not a complete recovery rehearsal or a guarantee of platform portability. Legacy format-1 Windows archives need the same Windows computer. New portable format-2 archives include password-encrypted key copies and re-protect them on the destination. External HTTPS/proxy certificates, services/tasks and environment secrets remain separate; borrower vaults still require their own private-list passphrase/recovery code. To recover under supervision, stop the server, keep current data separately, and use --unpack-complete-backup ARCHIVE NEW-FOLDER. Historical recovery rewinds accounts, passwords, deletions, revocations and loans; review before making it reachable. Settings category editors now keep their heading in normal page flow instead of overlapping form content when scrolled on mobile.

topics.title: Batch add books — scan a queue, review, save together
topics.body: Settings & Tools → Books & Organization → Batch add / CSV import (Android: Settings → Books & Organization). Queue ISBNs manually, with a keyboard scanner, or Continuous scan. Metadata looks up in the background while you continue scanning. Move the barcode out of view briefly before scanning an identical ISBN again; repeated scans are retained as separate candidate copies. Pause/resume or retry missing metadata, edit any row or add a book without an ISBN. Each batch holds up to 1000 rows and shows 25 rows at a time. Choose a collection, then Review batch. Correct errors or remove rows; mark Keep as additional physical copy for intentional duplicates. Confirm the reviewed list, then Save reviewed batch. The save adds all reviewed rows together or none; a concurrent change requires another review. A private pre-batch backup is saved. Existing catalog records are never replaced by this tool. Queues are unsaved work and are discarded on closing the tool. On Android, an interrupted save uses the existing Retry pending change flow; close the batch tool, resolve that change, then inspect the catalog before adding more. In the browser, Retry the same save confirms an interrupted operation using the same operation ID.

topics.title: Import CSV from another library app
topics.body: Use Batch add / CSV import → Choose CSV / Import library CSV. Supply a standard UTF-8 CSV or TSV export, at most 10 MB and 1000 book rows per reviewed batch. Comma, semicolon and tab separators, quoted commas/newlines and escaped quotes are supported. Column headers must be unique and every row must have matching columns. Check automatic mapping and choose columns yourself when names differ. Map title, author, ISBN/EAN, series, publisher, cover URL, room/bookcase/shelf, source catalog number and notes. Load mapped rows for review; this replaces only your unsaved queue after confirmation. ISBN-10/13 and whitespace/hyphens are normalized. Blank ISBN is allowed when a title is supplied. A new Carribrary copy number is assigned; source copy numbers and unsupported fields are retained in private import notes, never automatically applied as loans/accounts or personal reading. View/edit import notes under Edit book. Invalid rows and duplicate warnings must be resolved before saving. Browser Download review report or Android Save review report exports JSON errors/warnings. Generic mapped exports are supported; app-specific export variations need testing with a sample. Split larger exports into smaller batches. The JSON Restore tool is separate and replaces data; do not use it for CSV migration.

topics.title: Borrower renewals and librarian approval
topics.body: Signed-in borrowers open My loans → Request renewal → Confirm renewal request. Personal reading links and guests must ask the librarian instead. Default policy: requests require librarian approval, with 14 days per extension and at most two approved extensions per loan. The librarian can change those values under Settings & Tools → Borrowing & Reminders → Borrower renewals (Android: Settings → Borrowing & Reminders). Policy supports 1–90 days and 1–20 extensions per loan, optional automatic approval, or disabling requests. Returned loans, loans without a due date, an existing pending renewal, the renewal limit, or another open request/hold prevent renewal. For an overdue loan, a new request extends from today; otherwise it extends from the current due date. Pending proposals retain their proposed date when policy changes. The librarian reviews and approves or declines; approval rechecks eligibility and the original due date. A proposal whose new date has already passed must be declined and requested again. Returning the copy cancels its pending renewal. The due date changes only on approval; reading completion and returning a book remain separate. History is visible under My loans and the librarian renewal tool. Opening a link or page never renews a loan. The request bell continues to count book requests; check Borrower renewals separately for extension requests.

topics.title: Email password recovery for borrower accounts
topics.body: Configure SMTP in Automatic email reminders and enable the separate borrower email password recovery option. It is off by default and can be enabled without enabling scheduled reminders. Test SMTP using Send test to sending email. Borrowers choose Forgot your password? on sign-in, enter their username and request a link. The same generic response appears for unknown, blocked, non-email, disabled or undeliverable cases. Mail goes only to the address already recorded on the account, never an address typed into the reset form. The private link expires after 30 minutes, works once and is superseded by a newer reset; use it to choose a new 12–128 character password. Successful reset signs out existing account sessions. Requests are rate limited; repeated requests for the same account are suppressed for ten minutes. An interrupted server/mail delivery can require trying again after that interval. Pending jobs are not retained across a server restart. The librarian-issued reset-link fallback remains available. This resets only sign-in credentials: it cannot unlock encrypted reading/TBR/wishlist notes or replace a lost private-list passphrase/recovery code. Legacy personal records still awaiting encryption require librarian assistance.

topics.title: 2.0.43–2.0.45 data upgrade and recovery boundary
topics.body: Export a complete private backup before upgrading, including direct upgrades from earlier supported versions. Startup preserves books, borrowers, pairings, accounts and private vaults. The format-4 catalog migration protects ISBN-less books, private import notes and renewals. The new format-5 theme migration saves a separate pre-upgrade library backup and protects per-theme sidebar artwork. Credential format remains 2. Current program-only recovery is restricted to 2.0.45; older programs cannot preserve format-5 artwork. A supported historical complete archive can be verified, rehearsed and restored through Complete Backup Recovery using the new server. This rewinds historical account/device state and can lose later changes, so retained current data and local access review remain necessary. Android JSON restore accepts formats 1–5 with its existing replacement confirmation; complete archives remain separate. Rebuild packages from the same source; hosted iPhone PWA updates with its server, while Android needs an app update.

topics.title: Signed-in borrower catalog controls
topics.body: Signing in keeps the full catalog controls: search title, author, series, ISBN, copy ID or publisher; filter by Collection; sort by Title, Author, Series or Catalog number; choose 10, 25 or 50 per page. Changing a filter starts at page one. Catalog filters do not change My reading, My loans, requests or personal privacy. Your encrypted personal list can remain locked while browsing. The librarian has no new access to private reading data. These controls are on Catalog, not Account or My loans; My reading keeps its reading-status filter. The personal reading-link catalog also offers the same browsing controls.

topics.title: Companion dashboard, colored summaries and request bell
topics.body: Android Catalog and Home, and the iPhone/browser companion Catalog and Home, show the same four whole-library summary panels: Physical copies, Available, On loan and Active requests. Phone panels use two columns; wider screens use four. Available excludes loaned and held books. Active requests counts pending and approved requests, not closed requests; it is not an unread-message count. Catalog search and collection filters do not change these whole-library totals. Refresh updates the server snapshot; offline Android totals are cached and may be out of date. The header bell opens Requests with the current active count. It does not enable push notifications; those remain an optional separate setting. Android bottom navigation offers Home, Catalog, Loans, Reading and Settings; Borrowers and Requests remain available from Home and Settings. Home provides lending quick actions. Search from Android Home opens Catalog; iPhone header search opens Catalog on submit. All companions retain their existing pairing and catalog-first starting behavior. Native Android changes require the rebuilt app; hosted iPhone PWA changes arrive with the server update. Existing privacy, lending confirmation and account safeguards remain. The iPhone/browser companion has Home, Catalog, Loans, Reading and Settings in its bottom navigation; Borrowers remains on Home and under People & Access.

topics.title: Public welcome page: the library’s front door
topics.body: Opening the plain public server address now shows a branded welcome page. It follows the saved library name, logo, colors, tagline, encouraging saying and optional sidebar artwork. Artwork is therefore public branding: do not upload private information. The centered logo, library name and tagline sit above Browse the Catalog, Request a Book, Sign In and Get Help cards. Browse/Request open instructions for obtaining the private link; Sign In opens the borrower account and Help explains access. Librarian companion remains a separate header link. To browse or create an account, obtain the library’s shared link or QR from the librarian. The welcome page never includes the private catalog-sharing token, personal reading links, pairing codes, book records, contact details or account data. An invalid or revoked token still fails; the front door does not grant access. On the server computer the local address still requires administrator sign-in and opens Dashboard.

topics.title: Android Settings & Tools, reading and requests
topics.body: The Android bottom Settings button replaces the More label. Settings & Tools opens six categories: Library & Appearance; Books & Organization; Borrowing & Reminders; People & Access; Data & History; System & Advanced. Search all tools or open a category, then use Back to Settings & Tools. Colors/name/logo/sayings are under Library & Appearance. Borrowers and account approvals are under People & Access. Holds/batch lending, Requests and reminders are under Borrowing & Reminders. Backups, exports, restore, Recycle Bin, history and privacy controls are under Data & History. Manage library groups appearance, data/recovery and approved phones into expandable cards; opening its existing export/restore/device shortcuts retains their behavior and confirmations. Reading shows only the selected household reader’s TBR/finished totals; borrower private account lists remain encrypted and separate. Requests can show Open, All or Closed without changing server data. Book handover, account deletion, restore and revocation keep their original safeguards. Offline screens and manual scan entry remain available as before.

topics.title: Administrator and borrower starting pages
topics.body: The local server administrator opens Dashboard after sign-in and when reopening the main administration address. Catalog remains directly accessible from the sidebar or bottom navigation. Explicit Settings & Tools category links still open their requested page. Borrower accounts continue to open Catalog first, with My reading second. Paired companion devices keep their existing authentication and starting-page behavior.

topics.title: Borrower pages and iPhone companion layout
topics.body: The shared catalog, borrower sign-in and account use the library’s active colors, rounded cards and consistent headings. The shared catalog groups search, collection, sort and page size controls above book cards; availability badges distinguish Available, On hold and On loan. You may still request without creating an account. A successful request holds the copy pending librarian approval; the loan starts only at handover. Signed-in borrowers still open Catalog first; My reading holds encrypted TBR/reading, My loans holds borrowing history and requests, and Account groups private-list controls, installation, optional reminders, data/privacy, help and sign-out. Overview counts contain only the visible catalog or your own loans/requests; locked reading is not counted. Account deletion/history controls keep their previews, confirmations and scope. In the iPhone/browser librarian PWA, Settings & Tools home or People & Access shows This companion with optional request notifications and Sign out / unpair. Unpair affects this browser only and requires confirmation. Pairing, Help, scanning and manual entry retain their existing paths. Install from Safari Share → Add to Home Screen. Appearance changes need a reachable, updated server and a page refresh; no library data is cached by this redesign.

topics.title: Settings & Tools: six navigable category pages
topics.body: The sidebar keeps Dashboard, Catalog, Borrowers, Lending, Requests and Reading tracker. Settings & Tools replaces the old Backups, Devices, Library settings and All tools entries. Its homepage links to Library & Appearance; Books & Organization; Borrowing & Reminders; People & Access; Data & History; and System & Advanced. Each category has its own page, searchable cards and current saved values or explicit view/manage statuses. Search all settings by a tool name or purpose. Breadcrumb links, Back and browser Back/Forward navigate categories and individual editor pages. Most settings editors display in the page without a modal overlay. Dashboard shortcuts and everyday lending still open their existing operational dialogs. Complete backup, restore, history clearing and device/account removal keep their original protections. Navigation is blocked while a protected backup is preparing. Colors and custom themes now belong to Library & Appearance, not Catalog. Phone/PWA administrators use the bottom Settings button; native Android uses the same six categories under its Settings button. See the release tool inventory for each relocated function.

topics.title: Library names: automatic whole-word title fitting
topics.body: Library names wrap only at word boundaries beside the logo. The browser starts at the preferred title size and reduces it to a readable minimum until the longest word fits. If that is still too narrow, the logo moves above the name and the title is fitted to the full sidebar width. An exceptionally long unbroken name stays whole and can scroll horizontally within its own label; it never forces a single letter onto another line. This applies to all preset and saved custom themes and adapts on resize. Change the name under Settings & Tools → Library & Appearance → Library name.

topics.title: Catalog, Borrowers, Lending and Requests layout
topics.body: Catalog and Borrowers use explicit page headings, grouped search controls and consistent themed cards. Book actions remain visible; per-copy checkout/return, reading, About, editing, deletion and receipts keep their previous behavior. Borrowers shows contact details, consent and actual active-loan counts. Lending opens a wider workspace with Holds, Batch checkout, Batch return and Lending limits. Requests shows actual pending/approved/closed counts, a search field and status filter. Filters stay selected after decisions. Approval holds a copy; only physical handover starts its loan. Colors, saved themes and utility settings are under Settings & Tools. Destructive actions still require the existing confirmations.

topics.title: Custom library themes and the full color palette
topics.body: Web dashboard: open Settings & Tools → Library & Appearance → Theme & artwork or Theme & artwork. Colors are no longer in Catalog. Choose colors with the color picker or enter #RRGGBB hex values for banner/buttons/links, accent, page, cards/dialogs, soft highlights, borders, main text and secondary text. Enter a unique name and Save & use theme. Saved themes remain in Colors; choose one in the editor to update it, or choose New theme to save another. Saving affects the shared library, including borrower pages, sign-in, help and iPhone browser companion. Unsaved changes only appear in the preview. Contrast must reach 4.5:1 for normal text; use darker text/link colors and lighter backgrounds if saving is disabled. Presets remain available and switching does not delete custom themes. Names and palettes are included in private library backups; only the selected palette is exposed with public branding. On Android, Settings → Library & Appearance → Colors & custom themes opens presets, saved themes and the custom editor. Tap a color for hue/saturation/brightness sliders or hex entry. Presets and saved-theme selection change this phone; Save & use theme saves and activates a custom theme on the server. Settings → Apply selected theme to shared library publishes a selected preset. Existing phones keep their selected local theme. Android can select cached themes while offline; saving requires a server connection.

topics.title: Android companion: refreshed catalog and book options
topics.body: The top banner follows the phone’s selected theme and shows the library name, icon, saying and Help. Catalog shows library counts, search, Add book, Check out and Return. Filter & sort contains collection selection, ordering, 10/25/50 items per page and Bulk edit. Each card shows the cover, title, author, status and primary Check out or Return action. About opens book information. Book options contains Edit book, Borrowing receipt for active loans, and Move to Recycle Bin. Removal still requires confirmation; active loans remain protected. Bottom navigation is Catalog, Loans, Reading and Settings. More groups people/lending, sharing/collections and settings/backups. Android’s bundled Help uses the selected phone theme. Existing pairing, ISBN scanning and optional copy labels keep their behavior.

topics.title: Versioned source downloads and building updates
topics.body: Download the versioned Carribrary-2.0.39-source.zip source archive. It extracts into Carribrary-2.0.39, containing home-library-native and the matching help guide. Keep that top-level versioned folder; do not merge it with old sources or an installed library. Run the existing Build-Carribrary launcher inside home-library-native. No installer or APK is built automatically by the source download. GitHub’s standard Download ZIP still uses Carribrary-main; rename its extracted top-level folder to Carribrary-2.0.39 before building, or use the versioned archive provided with the source handoff. Existing signing keys must be reused privately for Android updates; do not generate a replacement identity. After upgrading, refresh/reopen web/PWA pages and install your newly built Android update. Custom themes are additive on upgrade from older releases, but older programs cannot read them; program-only recovery for this source release accepts 2.0.39 programs only. Complete backups remain the recovery path for historical installations; do not restore old data over a current library merely to change colors. The builder can reuse .build-tools from the new versioned folder, its parent, or a sibling Carribrary-main folder; CARRIBRARY_TOOLS selects another private compiler-cache folder. This does not merge source versions or move old folders.

topics.title: Start here
topics.body: The Android companion is for the household librarian. Pair it with your Windows, Linux or Raspberry Pi server using Paired admin phones. Borrowers use Create account / Sign in on the shared library page; they do not need the admin companion. The server must remain on and reachable.

topics.title: Administrator dashboard and navigation
topics.body:
The admin web dashboard and paired iPhone/browser companion have a responsive layout. Desktop uses a stationary left menu; on phones use Home, Catalog, Borrowers and Settings at the bottom. Local administrators start on Dashboard; already paired companions keep their Catalog starting view in this iteration. Home opens the whole-library dashboard. Its counts include all active collections, unlike a filtered catalog. Available excludes copies on loan and held copies. Recent requests includes resolved history; Active requests counts only pending and approved requests.

Quick Actions are Add Book, Create Hold, Batch Checkout and Backup Now. They open existing workflows; Backup Now opens backup options and does not create a backup until you choose and confirm an option. A hold does not start a loan. Confirm handover only when the borrower receives the books. System Status shows connection and links to the existing device, backup and reminder checks; the links do not mean a backup or delivery succeeded.

More / All tools keeps printing, numbering, requests, holds, accounts, reading, sharing, exports, recovery and setup available. Library settings retains your saved name, custom icon, sayings and colors. The sidebar repeats your existing encouraging saying; leave it blank in Library settings to hide it. Sidebar artwork opens a PNG upload and Remove artwork option. There is no built-in decoration. Upload your own PNG under 10 MB; recommended size 512 × 256 pixels with transparency. Larger images are fitted without cropping. The saved result is limited to 350 KB and is included in library exports/backups. Removing it clears it for this library and paired browser companions. Artwork never blocks controls and is hidden on narrow or short screens. Borrower pages and the native Android layout are unchanged in this first redesign iteration. Paired devices keep their existing authentication.

On desktop, the search box at the top searches the catalog: type a title, author, series, ISBN or copy ID and press Enter. The dashboard uses your saved library name, subtitle, icon and color theme; it does not install Queen B branding for other households. Sidebar artwork remains optional and is uploaded separately in Library settings. On phones Quick Actions follows Recent requests, while Home, Catalog, Borrowers and Settings stay reachable at the bottom. Native Android uses matching native cards and six Settings & Tools categories.

topics.title: Borrower app: Catalog, My reading, My loans and Account
topics.body:
After an approved borrower signs in, Catalog opens first. Search and browse books, request an available copy, or open About this book. On phones use Catalog, My reading, My loans and Account at the bottom; on larger screens the same navigation is above the content. My account in the header also opens Account. Your current search stays when switching views.

My reading is your encrypted personal TBR/history. If it is locked, unlock it with your private passphrase or cancel and continue browsing. The separate passphrase is not required for catalog browsing or borrowing requests. Account → Private reading & wishlist has lock/unlock, private wishlist, clear finished reading and encrypted personal export/restore. Personal reading remains private from the librarian; operational library loans and requests remain visible to them.

My loans includes My book requests. Open requests have a count in the navigation. Request cancellation still requires confirmation and releases only its own hold; librarian approval is not a checkout. Refresh reloads the current state without changing views. Account contains install/Home screen, optional due-date notifications, account help, Data & privacy (clear completed history and account deletion) and Sign out. A pending account can still use install/help, sign out and its deletion tools before approval. Native Android administrator layout is unchanged by this borrower web/PWA iteration.

topics.title: Borrower account deletion: which username to enter
topics.body: In the borrower web/PWA, open Account → Data & privacy → My data & privacy → Delete my account. Choose the data scope and preview it. The confirmation field shows the exact sign-in username separately from your display/reader name. Type that sign-in username; the borrower page ignores capitalization, surrounding spaces and one optional leading @. It does not autofill the confirmation. Your current password is still required, with its exact capitalization and spacing. Changing deletion scope clears the username/password fields and requires a fresh preview. A different username, wrong password, stale preview or protected active loans still prevents deletion. Administrator account-deletion tools retain their own existing confirmation rules.

topics.title: Optional sidebar artwork
topics.body: No illustration is hardcoded or installed by default. Open Settings & Tools → Library & Appearance → Full sidebar overlay. Upload your own PNG, review the portrait preview and Save artwork. Recommended canvas: 512 × 1536 pixels. The input must be under 10 MB and at most 8192 pixels per side; it is fitted without cropping into a transparent 512 × 1536 PNG, maximum 2 MB after resizing. The saved image fills the entire desktop sidebar beneath navigation. A dark readability layer keeps names, icons and buttons legible; the image cannot intercept clicks. Older 512 × 256 artwork remains accepted but may crop when covering the full sidebar; re-upload a portrait original for best results. Remove artwork restores the plain theme. Artwork stays separate from the icon, colors and saying, is included in library exports/backups, and follows paired browser companions. The sidebar is hidden on narrow screens. Native Android has no desktop sidebar. The same optional artwork is also public branding on the plain-address welcome page. Never upload private information; removing it removes it from all banners after refresh. The same saved image appears cropped and tinted in borrower headers, the librarian PWA and Android banner. A plain theme clears it; selecting a saved theme restores its own artwork. Refresh browser pages or Android after changing the library appearance.

topics.title: Local administrator sign-in and recovery
topics.body:
Carribrary now requires its own administrator sign-in on the server computer, even when Windows is signed in. This protects the local dashboard and administrative API. An update keeps your books, borrowers, settings and approved phones. Already paired Android and iPhone/browser companions keep their existing access without another password screen. Borrower sign-in and private reading-vault credentials are separate.

On first open, choose an administrator username and a password of 12–128 characters. The page shows the private local-admin-setup.txt file location in your server data folder. On Windows, select Start → Carribrary → Administrator access and approve the Windows administrator prompt; Copy setup code, then Open local sign-in. The installer also offers this private code when you finish and open the library. This helper only reads an existing code; it does not reset credentials or sign you in. Alternatively open the file using an authorized server administrator account. Paste the code into the setup form and confirm your password. Being the first visitor to the page does not grant administrator access. Do not send the setup code, password or recovery code to support.

Save the new recovery code privately, preferably away from the server computer, then select I have saved this code safely → Open library. Signing out ends this local browser session. Local sessions expire after 30 minutes idle, eight hours total, or a server restart. A fresh private/InPrivate browser must sign in independently.

If you forget your local password, select Recover local administrator access and enter your saved recovery code with new credentials. This consumes the code, creates a replacement recovery code and signs out all local dashboard sessions; existing paired phones stay approved. It does not reset borrower passwords or unlock private reading vaults. If every recovery code is lost, stop Carribrary and run the included server executable with --prepare-local-admin-recovery using the same data-folder configuration. This advanced, stopped-server procedure writes a new private one-time code without deleting data. Restart, open local recovery and use the code. The procedure is blocked while that data folder is in use. Never delete the credential file as a recovery method. An already authorized companion can also prepare a setup/recovery code through the protected server operation; a dedicated companion recovery button is not yet supplied in this repair pass.

Revoking a phone or paired browser rejects its next server request immediately, including requests on a reused connection. It does not erase a previously downloaded offline catalog. Disabling an account, local sign-out and unpairing a device are distinct actions.

The local dashboard uses loopback HTTP only; its HttpOnly, SameSite session cookie is not a public HTTPS companion credential. Do not forward its port or put it behind a public proxy. Public and native companions retain their existing secure connections. The multi-administrator update safely upgrades the protected credentials while keeping your original username, password and recovery code. Earlier programs cannot decrypt the new credential format. Program-only recovery is restricted to 2.0.36; keep a complete pre-update backup for supervised recovery to an earlier release. Retain complete private backups and use supervised recovery across this security boundary. On Flatpak, Stop server now opens the local browser, requires login if needed, and asks you to confirm stopping before shutting down.

More than one person can sign in. Open Settings & Tools → People & Access → Dashboard administrators → Add administrator. Each person has their own username, password, recovery code and local sessions. All dashboard administrators have full library-management privileges, including managing additional administrators; add only trusted people. The primary account cannot be removed, and you cannot remove the account you are using. Up to 100 dashboard accounts are supported. Accounts can use different browser profiles or private windows simultaneously. On a shared browser sign out before another person signs in.

Give a newly created administrator their username, initial password and one-time-displayed recovery code privately. They can choose Change my password after local sign-in using their current password. It renews that session and ends their other local sessions. Reset password or Remove administrator immediately ends the affected account’s local sessions; other administrators stay signed in. Additional administrators can recover their own account with their username and recovery code. Primary account/server-owner recovery still ends all local sessions. Dashboard account removal does not delete a borrower/reader or revoke independent paired-device tokens; revoke those separately under Paired phones / iPhone companion. Borrower sign-ins never grant admin access. Existing paired companions keep token access without another password login.

topics.title: Complete server data backup — recommended before updates
topics.body:
On the server open Backups → Create complete backup. On Android open Settings → Data & History → Complete server data backup. The iPhone admin PWA uses the same server Backups dialog. Choose a backup password of 12–128 characters, confirm it, and save the .carribrary-backup file. Keep the password safely and store a copy on another drive. It cannot be reset. The server briefly pauses changes, captures consistent SQLite snapshots including committed WAL data, then resumes automatically; you do not have to stop it or copy hidden folders. Confirm that the download finishes before closing the page/app. Use the server computer for large archives.

Includes current library/loan records, borrowers, sign-in accounts, encrypted borrower vaults, pairing identities, keyring, notification/reminder saved settings and saved application configuration. Complete snapshots contain private records and server credentials, so they are password-encrypted. Borrower private reading stays encrypted inside the archive and still needs each borrower's own private passphrase/recovery code. This does not give administrators access to borrower personal reading.

Current-data limit: 2 GB and 10,000 files. Earlier automatic backups/recovery points, program binaries/installers, external HTTPS/Caddy certificates, operating-system service/task definitions and settings supplied only through environment variables are not included. Keep those separately if needed. This is a complete current server-DATA backup, not a full computer image or guaranteed cross-platform migration. Legacy format-1 Windows archives require the same Windows computer; new format-2 portable archives support replacement-computer recovery.

The smaller Backups → Export library JSON option includes books and administrative lending records, but excludes credentials, pairing keys and borrower private vaults. Restore library export accepts that JSON only. It cannot restore a complete encrypted server-data archive.

The independent Complete Backup Recovery application-menu wizard now provides guided verification, isolated testing and confirmed restoration (see its Help topic). The developer offline utility remains available: stop Carribrary, keep the current data folder separately, then use the included HomeLibrary.Server --unpack-complete-backup ARCHIVE NEW-FOLDER command. It asks privately for the backup password, verifies authenticated encryption, inventory hashes and SQLite integrity, and unpacks only into a new folder. It never overwrites an existing folder or running library. Follow RECOVERY-READ-ME.txt in the recovered folder: restore the entire data folder together, including all databases/keyrings; use matching or compatible server programs; review supplied configuration separately. Get recovery help if unsure. On Flatpak, use the bundled Linux recovery instructions to grant access only to the archive/output folders for this offline command. Never put the backup password in a command argument or send it to support.

Copies outside Carribrary and downloaded archives can retain information deleted later. Keep these backups private and remove unwanted copies yourself. Forgotten archive passwords cannot be recovered. If a download fails, delete the incomplete downloaded file and retry. Internal temporary snapshots are removed after delivery or normal failure; a machine crash can leave an unfinished .complete-backup-* folder inside the protected data folder. Stop the server before cleaning up those unfinished temporary folders.

If a borrower still has legacy private reading records awaiting encryption, complete downloading is blocked until that borrower finishes private-list encryption setup. This avoids exposing legacy personal notes through an admin download. Ordinary library JSON export remains available and continues to omit those records.

Restoring an earlier complete snapshot rewinds account deletions, passwords, device revocations and lending history. Review accounts and paired devices before making the restored server reachable. Compatible program-only recovery keeps current data instead.

topics.title: Permanent copy identity and upgrading to 2.0.31
topics.body:
Each physical copy has a permanent internal identity separate from its visible BK catalog number. Editing, restarting, current-format backup/restore and Recycle Bin recovery preserve it. Reusing an available BK number creates a distinct copy identity. The optional QR labels use this permanent identity; ISBN/EAN and manual circulation still work without labels.

Before updating, create a complete private backup. The new server migrates library format 1 or 2 to format 3 and saves an encrypted pre-change administrative library backup. That administrative export is not a complete account/key/vault backup. Existing identities and numbers stay. Older JSON exports can be imported; identities absent from them cannot recreate original identities they never contained.

Versions 2.0.30 and earlier cannot open the upgraded library. Do not downgrade. Windows program recovery supports 2.0.36–2.0.39 multi-administrator credentials only; earlier programs cannot read the upgraded protected credentials and cannot be offered for program-only recovery; old private recovery points remain retained but cannot be offered across this data-format boundary. Cross-format recovery requires supervised use of a complete pre-upgrade backup. Update the server first, then companions; pairing remains valid.

topics.title: Home Library is now Carribrary
topics.body:
Carribrary is the new product name for Home Library. Install the new server and companion updates over your existing versions; export a backup first and update the server before the phone app. Do not uninstall or clear app data. Your library name (such as Queen B’s Library), books, borrowers, accounts, holds, reading lists, custom icon, settings and phone pairing remain yours. The existing book-and-house symbol is still the app icon; launcher labels, installer names and help now use Carribrary.

Windows updates reuse the registered install folder and replace the old desktop, Start menu and startup shortcuts. Windows Services shows Carribrary with the internal name HomeLibraryNative. Android keeps the same application ID and signing identity, so the APK updates the existing app. Linux keeps the same Flatpak ID and stable branch; Raspberry Pi keeps the home-library-server package and home-library service. Existing technical file names, data folders, scheduled task names and connection protocols may still contain Home Library or home-library for compatibility. There is no need to move data or pair again.

Browser apps keep your library’s own name and custom icon. Reopen or refresh after updating the server. Installed Home-screen labels and icons may take time to refresh; if needed remove only the shortcut and add it again. Never clear app storage merely to refresh an icon.

topics.title: Find your way around
topics.body: Catalog lists books. Loans shows checked-out copies. Reading has personal reading lists. Settings opens six Settings & Tools categories. Search all tools or open a category and use Back to return. Help is always available in the top banner.

topics.title: Add books and find covers
topics.body: Catalog → Add book → scan the existing ISBN or enter it → Look up book details → check the title, author and collection → Save. For missing images use Search Books for a cover. Review different-edition suggestions, choose Use this cover, then Save. Google Books is optional and configured in the server’s Settings & Tools → System & Advanced. Provider errors may require another try.

topics.title: Scan, check out and return
topics.body: Use the book’s printed ISBN barcode, an optional BK copy label, or manual entry. Checkout selects an available copy; return selects a checked-out copy. When several copies match, choose the correct one. Choose the borrower and dates, then confirm. Custom labels are optional. Reading status does not check books out or return them.

topics.title: Camera trouble
topics.body: Allow camera access when prompted. Choose the rear camera that focuses best and save it as the default. Use steady light, keep the barcode flat and move the phone slightly farther away. Manual ISBN/copy-ID entry always works. The server must use HTTPS for browser camera access.

topics.title: Borrowers, requests and receipts
topics.body: Settings → People & Access → Borrowers adds people you lend to. Requests go to the inbox for review. Approve a request, then hand over/check out the book when ready. Approval alone does not create a loan. Borrowing receipt prepares a text or email in your messaging app; you choose whether to send it.

topics.title: Reading lists
topics.body: Admin Reading manages household profiles that are not linked to borrowers. Those household profiles are shared with paired admins. Borrower personal reading, ratings, dates, notes, TBR and private wishlists use the borrower account’s encrypted vault and are not visible or editable in admin screens, phone snapshots or administrative exports. Borrowers use their account in a browser/PWA. Reading status remains independent of lending. A private reader can keep encrypted book details after a catalog copy is removed; a reused Copy ID with a different ISBN does not attach the old notes to the new book.

topics.title: Library QR, personal QR and accounts
topics.body: Share library / QR opens the public catalog. Guests can browse and request without an account. Accounts are needed for borrower-private lists: the librarian approves the operational borrower link, but the borrower sets a separate private-list passphrase and recovery code. Admin pairing QR codes grant library administration, not decryption of borrower personal records. Personal reading links for admin-managed unlinked household profiles remain capability links; anyone with such a link can use that household list, including an admin who issued it. Older borrower reading QR links no longer open borrower personal records; use a borrower account instead.

topics.title: Approve and recover an account
topics.body: Approve pending borrower accounts and link the correct operational borrower, or create one. Account sign-in recovery and private-list recovery are separate. A librarian can issue a one-use, 30-minute password-reset link after private reading is encrypted; it restores sign-in only, not the private-list passphrase or recovery code. Reset links are blocked while older personal records await encryption. Existing reset tokens and sign-in sessions are revoked once on upgrade to the new privacy model. There is no automatic email recovery service. An existing private profile cannot be assigned to a different account. If a deleted account’s borrower is approved for a new account, the new account starts a fresh private profile and does not inherit the previous private list; the owner can restore an encrypted personal backup with its own passphrase or code. When reapproving an existing account, select its correct operational borrower; its own hidden private profile stays attached to the same account. If the old borrower was removed and no replacement is selected, approval creates a replacement borrower. This does not unlock the encrypted list or transfer it to anyone else.

topics.title: Collections, filters and colors
topics.body: Catalog → Filter & sort reveals collection, sort order and page size. Settings → Books & Organization manages collections. Settings → Library & Appearance → Colors & custom themes changes this phone’s theme. Library name & sayings changes the shared library banner. Collections organize books; they are not separate access-controlled libraries. The server’s Settings & Tools → Library & Appearance → Theme & artwork selector now saves the shared library palette, including borrower sign-in, registration, account and installed pages. On Android, Colors still sets your phone’s preference; Manage library → Apply selected theme to shared library publishes it to the server and borrower pages. Refresh open pages after a change. Legacy installations adopt the existing server browser’s selected palette when opened after updating.

topics.title: Backups, privacy and moving servers
topics.body:
Administrative Export backup includes catalog books, private shelf locations, Books to buy, borrowers, operational loans/requests and admin-managed household reading. It excludes borrower personal profiles, reading entries and encrypted vault contents. Keep this administrative export private: contacts and lending records still belong there. Administrative Restore preserves existing borrower private records rather than replacing them.

Borrowers use Export encrypted personal backup and keep the separate recovery code. A library JSON export is not a complete backup of sign-ins, pairing or personal vaults. For a complete host backup, stop the server and protect a copy of the entire data directory, including the account database, encrypted vault database and keyrings. On a new account/server, set up a new private list, then restore the owner’s encrypted personal backup using its original private passphrase or recovery code. Previous exports and safety backups may contain earlier unencrypted reading records; encryption cannot retroactively change existing copies.

topics.title: Offline, remote access and updates
topics.body: Offline mode shows the encrypted cached library; changes need a connection. Refresh after the server returns. Resolve Retry pending change before submitting another action. Remote browser accounts require your public HTTPS sharing address; no extra ports are needed beyond existing HTTPS sharing. Keep the server on. Install updates over the existing server/app, keeping data, rather than uninstalling first.

topics.title: Windows server: install, open and update
topics.body:
Install the Carribrary Windows installer on the computer that will hold your library. It runs the Carribrary service in the background and creates desktop/Start menu shortcuts. You do not need Node.js or a separate .NET installation. Open the Carribrary shortcut to administer your books. The normal admin address is http://localhost:4173 on the server computer.

Before an update, export a library backup. Run the newer installer over the current installation; do not uninstall or delete the data folder first. Close old manually started server windows so they cannot occupy the same ports. Install the matching Android APK over the existing phone app to preserve pairing.

topics.title: Start, stop and restart the server
topics.body:
Windows: open the Windows Services app, find Carribrary (HomeLibraryNative), then use Start, Stop or Restart. The native service is designed to start automatically with Windows. Closing the admin browser window does not stop it. If Windows reports a service error, use the installed diagnostics/repair tools and keep the diagnostic text for support; do not delete library data.

Linux Flatpak: launch Carribrary from the application menu. Closing the browser keeps the server running. The launcher’s Stop library server action stops it. Desktop logout or reboot also stops it; use desktop Autostart if you want it available after login.

Raspberry Pi: the DEB installs a systemd service named home-library. A desktop service manager can start, stop or restart it. The service normally starts at boot. Keep the Pi powered and connected while phones or borrowers need access.

topics.title: Linux and Raspberry Pi installation
topics.body:
Linux desktop: open the x86_64 Flatpak bundle in Discover or another Flatpak installer, then launch Carribrary from the application menu. Install Flatpak support through your software manager if needed. On a fresh install, log out/in if the menu entry is missing.

Raspberry Pi 4 or 5: use 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS and the ARM64 DEB package. Open it in the system’s package installer. The Pi version is the library server, not the Android APK.
